contract: Pure upper bound, as far as recordings through OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, routed to Anthropic, show under a named assumption (not proved), before the call, for the input tokens of one integration/ai-text request to Anthropic: Elzoo.AiTokenCount.Anthropic.estimate/1 decodes the request bytes with Elzoo.AiText.Request.decode/1 and returns size = 3 * canonical bytes, plus 1,024 when the request has a tool, with unit :tokens, direction :upper_bound, provider_id, model_id and estimator elzoo/ai-token-count/anthropic-bytes version 1 (the fields of a workflow/context-selection window); refuses the decoder's reasons unchanged, an output_schema as :unsupported_feature and a model that pinned llm_db does not know for Anthropic as :unknown_model. Not a token count and not a usage fact.
limits: The factor 3 rests on Monitored recordings of one model (claude-haiku-5-5) on one day, recorded through OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, routed to Anthropic; not a proof, not the provider's Contract. The tokenizer is not published: a text pattern that was not tried, a new model or a new tokenizer can break the bound.
No claim for another model, a direct call to Anthropic, or a request feature that no fixture covers (reasoning, cache hint, stop sequences); a request with an output_schema is refused.

Not exact and not tight: on the fixtures size is 1.74 to 29.72 times the reported prompt input, about nine times on ordinary prose. No claim about output tokens, cost, cache savings or a rate limit; the value is not a usage fact and is not for billing.

Known models are those of the pinned llm_db 2026.11.0 catalogue as packaged; a host that filters or replaces it changes which models are known. A caller reads a model's limit from LLMDB.model/2 itself; this Piece wraps neither.

integration/ai-text-anthropic and plug are test-only dependencies (group fixture_matches_adapter captures the adapter's body through its :plug test transport); the lib file uses neither and no test calls the network.

grounding.claim: Seven listed groups on the committed fixtures, no network. fixtures_upper_bound: for each of the fifteen fixtures, size is at least input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens of its recorded response. observed_error_stated: the README row of each fixture (canonical bytes, reported, size, size / reported to two decimals), the smallest ratio 1.74 and the largest 29.72 and the provenance wording are computed again from the fixtures. fixture_matches_adapter: for each fixture the body that integration/ai-text-anthropic sends (translate/2 with a plug, call/2 with a stub credential) equals the upstream fixture without its provider member, as decoded JSON. unknown_model_refused: claude-no-such-model-9, gpt-4o-mini and anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5 are refused :unknown_model; the alias claude-sonnet-4-5 is accepted with model_id unchanged. tools_and_system_counted: a first tool adds 3 * its canonical bytes + 1,024, a second tool 3 * its canonical bytes; a system message adds at least 3 * its text bytes; key order and whitespace do not change the result. never_exact: each result has exactly the seven keys and direction :upper_bound; only estimate/1 is exported; each refusal is reached with no number; README and manifest call the value an upper bound. no_network: source audit of the lib file and of the manifest providers. Negative controls: factor 1 fails fixtures_upper_bound on four fixtures; tools left out fail tools_and_system_counted. Finite scenarios, not proofs.

Fifteen fixtures and a probe table of 465 further requests (464 with usage), recorded 2026-11-13 through OpenRouter's Anthropic-compatible endpoint, routed to Anthropic (provider pinned to Anthropic, no fallback), for claude-haiku-5-5; the file lists each difference from a direct call and what was not recorded. Observations of one model on one day, not a proof.
llm_db 2026.11.0 LLMDB.model/2 resolves Anthropic model ids and aliases from the snapshot packaged inside the library, with no network.

No request gives more than three reported tokens for each canonical byte; Anthropic's tool-use system prompt stays at most 1,024 tokens (its table of tool use system prompt tokens, page Tool use with Claude, section Pricing, read 2026-11-13, had 804 as its largest value); OpenRouter passes the request body and Anthropic's usage on unchanged.

telemetry.contract: Pure function: emits no event, measurement or trace; the caller owns instrumentation.

config.contract: No setting: the factor 3, the 1,024 for tools and the estimator version are fixed in the code; a change of the rule is a new estimator_version.

control.contract: No process, lifecycle or state to control: one call returns one value.
